title: EU AI Act Article 6 — Classification Rules for High-Risk AI Systems | Council of AI Regulatory Watch
context: 2026-08-31 engine cycle — answer-first seed covering the gateway classification article that determines which AI systems fall under the EU AI Act's high-risk obligations; timed to the Aug 2026 grace-period deadline for existing high-risk systems
body: Article 6 of the EU AI Act is the classification gate: it determines whether an AI system is 'high-risk' and therefore subject to the Act's full conformity assessment, risk management, data governance, transparency, human oversight, and accuracy requirements. An AI system is classified as high-risk if it meets EITHER of two conditions. Condition (a): the system is a safety component of a product covered by EU harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I (machinery, toys, lifts, medical devices, radio equipment, etc.), OR the system is itself such a product, AND the product is required to undergo a third-party conformity assessment under that legislation. Condition (b): the system is listed in Annex III, which covers eight areas: biometrics (remote biometric identification, emotion recognition), critical infrastructure (safety components in management and operation), education and vocational training (access determination, assessment of learning), employment and worker management (recruitment, promotion, task allocation, monitoring), access to essential services (creditworthiness, risk assessment for life/health insurance, emergency triage), law enforcement (individual risk assessments, polygraphs, evidence reliability, profiling, crime analytics), migration and border management (risk assessments, security checks, examination of applications), and administration of justice (judicial research, interpretation of law). However, Article 6(3) provides a derogation: a system listed in Annex III is NOT high-risk if it does not pose a significant risk of harm to the health, safety, or fundamental rights of natural persons, including by not materially influencing the outcome of decision-making. Providers must document any derogation claim and notify authorities. The classification timeline matters: general-purpose AI rules took effect 2 February 2025; high-risk system obligations in Annex III take effect 2 August 2026. Systems already on the market before 2 August 2026 get a transitional period until 2 August 2030 — but only if they are subject to a new contract or significant design change. The practical question every compliance team is asking in August 2026: does your system fall through the Article 6 gate, and if so, have you booked your notified body slot?
references: EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689), Articles 6, 43, 48 and Annexes I, III
